content:
Past week has seen a flurry of rumors about Apple’s upcoming built-in camera AirPods. Here’s a roundup of everything we’ve learned this week about the camera-equipped AirPods Pro.

Latest news on camera-equipped AirPods Pro

It all started on Monday, when someone spotted built-in camera AirPods in a video within the macOS 26.7 beta. In the clip, a person wearing AirPods Pro holds up a book and asks Siri to use Visual Intelligence to note down that book.

In the video, the camera-equipped AirPods Pro looks almost identical to the existing AirPods Pro 3.

Apart from the video, there are also plenty of code references related to built-in camera AirPods in macOS 26.7, further revealing how it works.

According to code seen by 9to5Mac, Apple will use a new framework called AccessorySensorMgrd to control image capture and other functions of the built-in camera AirPods. In the code, Apple refers to this camera sensor as the “Kino Sensor”.

  • Each AirPods Pro earbud has its own camera, and the two sides will pair up to work together and capture synchronously. The AccessorySensorMgrd framework will combine the images from both sides. However, if only one side captures an image, the framework will generate a blank corresponding image.
  • macOS 26.7 mentions two “capture modes”: active and passive. Active mode appears to capture one image from each AirPod, or provide a “capture rate” to continuously transmit images at a specified rate.
  • The framework tracks multiple factors, including image width and height, pixel binning, left/right X/Y offset, and more.
  • The framework also mentions that AirPods Pro will have a privacy indicator light that illuminates when the camera is capturing images.

Meanwhile, a MacRumors forum user also found some details about the AirPods Pro camera resolution:

Active capture mode starts with a 640×640 image and ultimately outputs a processed 1024×1024 image. In other words, the sampled image data is about 0.4 megapixels, while the output image is slightly over 1 megapixel. There is also a lower-resolution passive capture mode that starts capturing at 320×320 and returns either 320×320 or 512×512 output depending on the capture mode. The above is the resolution for capture; the physical sensor’s native resolution could be even larger.

The forum member also provided more details about “passive mode”, described as “lower resolution and supporting ambient awareness”. macOS 26 lists five possible scenarios that trigger passive capture:

  • Ambient voice
  • Audio scene change
  • Posture change
  • Head turn
  • “Shape zone, i.e., the user has moved out of a defined spatial radius.”

Release date of built-in camera AirPods

With related videos and code references appearing in the macOS 26.7 beta, it immediately sparked speculation that this product is about to launch, possibly as early as next month’s Apple event alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra.

However, according to a Bloomberg report, that is not the case. In a report on Wednesday, Mark Gurman pointed out that the built-in camera AirPods remain on track for a 2027 launch.

Gurman explained that Apple is internally developing two versions of this product:

  • B790: The version shown in the video. Essentially an improved version of AirPods Pro 3, but with a camera added.
  • B798: The next-generation AirPods (such as AirPods Pro 4), also with a camera added.

It is currently unclear which version Apple will ultimately release, but in any case, it won’t arrive until at least next year.

Bloomberg’s report also reiterated that the AirPods Pro camera will not be used for taking photos and videos. Instead, it is designed to “scan the surrounding environment and provide contextual information to the Siri digital assistant and other AI tools”.

Summary

In summary, this week has indeed released a lot of new information about the built-in camera AirPods, including details about its features and how it works.

What do you think about Apple adding a camera to AirPods Pro? Do you think it’s a good idea? Feel free to share your thoughts with us in the comments section.
